assets.label: Figure 13.1
assets.caption: Figure 13.1 The importance of linearity in the parent-offspring regression. If this regression is nonlinear, different subsets of the population with the same mean can have different offspring means. Suppose equal numbers of parents with values  $ z_a $ and  $ z_b $ are chosen. If we denote the expected value of offspring from parents with value  $ z_x $ by  $ E[z \mid z_x] $, the offspring mean in this case is given by  $ (E[z \mid z_a] + E[z \mid z_b]) / 2 $. In contrast, choosing parents all with value  $ (z_a + z_b) / 2 $ gives the same parental mean as in the case of mixed parents, and hence the same  $ S $, but the expected offspring mean is now  $ E[z \mid (z_a + z_b) / 2] $, which, as shown above, can deviate considerably from  $ E[z \mid z_a] + E[z \mid z_b] / 2 $ when nonlinearity is significant.

assets.label: Figure 13.2
assets.caption: Figure 13.2 The general selection problem: The ultimate goal is to predict the selection response in some response trait (whose values are denoted by y), based on the values of a potentially different—but genetically correlated—selected trait (whose values are denoted by z). The values of the selected trait are measured on one set of individuals (indexed by  $ x_i $). For example, the value  $ (z_x) $ of the selected trait in individual x may be an index that weights  $ x' $'s value for the response trait, as well as the values of the response trait in several of  $ x' $'s relatives. In the figure,  $ x_3 $ has the highest value of the selected trait, but instead of using  $ x_3 $ as a parent for the next generation (which would correspond to individual selection), we instead use a relative,  $ \mathcal{R} $, of  $ x_3 $, with o denoting an offspring from  $ \mathcal{R} $. The covariance required for predicting the mean change in the response trait is  $ \sigma(z_x, y_0) $, namely, the covariance between the selection trait value  $ (z_x) $ in individual x and the response trait value  $ (y_0) $ in the offspring of parent  $ \mathcal{R} $. Under our infinitesimal assumption that the expected value of an offspring is the average of the two parental breeding values, this covariance is also  $ \sigma[z_x, A_y(\mathcal{R})/2] $, half the covariance between the phenotypic value of the selection trait in x and the breeding value for the response trait in  $ x' $'s relative,  $ \mathcal{R} $.

assets.label: Table 13.2
assets.caption: Table 13.2 Summary of various factors complicating the prediction of short-term selection response in the phenotypic mean, even assuming all regressions are linear and considering just a single generation of selection from an unselected base population. Short-term response specifically refers to conditions where the effects of any allele-frequency change on the additive variance are negligible. Models of long-term response (Chapters 25–28) relax this restriction.
rows: Major gene with dominance (Chapter 6; LW Chapter 17)
Can generate a nonlinear parent-offspring regression.
The component of response due to epistasis is transient. Parent-offspring covariance overestimates permanent response.
The component of response due to correlated environmental effects is transient.
The potential for complicated lags in response—the mean changes unpredictably after selection is relaxed. Possibility of reversed response.
Changes the additive genetic variance. Directional selection generates negative gametic-phase disequilibrium, reducing $ h^{2} $ and slowing response.
Generates gametic-phase disequilibrium, which either enhances (positive correlation between mates) or retards (negative correlation between mates) response.
A significant change in the environment can obscure the true amount of genetic change.
Generates variance in the short-term response.
Environmental factors can influence both the trait and fitness, confounding both the nature of selection and the true amount of genetic change.
Trait influenced by both direct and social components from group members. A decline in the mean social value can swamp an increase in mean direct value. Possibility of reversed response.
Response depends on additional variance components that are difficult to estimate ( $ \sigma_{D1}^{2}, \sigma_{AD1}, \text{etc} $). Response has permanent and transient components.
Several generations are required to propagate genetic change uniformly through the population.
Response completely unpredictable unless selection on correlated characters accounted for. Possibility of reversed response.

Possibility of nonlinear parent-offspring regressions. Often treated as a correlated character problem, with traits measured in different environments treated as correlated traits. Possibility of reversed response.

Robertson-Price恒等式 $S=\sigma(w,z)$（方程式6.10）
育种值的概念及其在响应中的作用（方程式6.25a）
亲本-子代回归的线性假设

prerequisites.concept_title: Chapter 6 · Theorems of Natural Selection: Results of Price, Fisher, and Robertson
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 第13章在多个小节（如第13.2节、第13.7节）中明确引用第6章的Price方程、Robertson-Price恒等式以及相关方程，以建立育种者方程和响应预测的理论基础。

prerequisites.title: Chapter 3 · Covariance, Regression, and Correlation
prerequisites.why_needed: 当前章节的育种者方程和选择响应依赖于协方差和回归的概念，这些内容在源章节中详细讲解。
key_points: 协方差衡量两个变量线性关系的方向和强度。
回归系数表示自变量变化时因变量的平均变化。
亲子回归系数是遗传力估计的基础。
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前章节多次提及亲子回归和协方差，这些正是源章节的核心内容。

prerequisites.title: Chapter 4 · Breeding Values and Infinitesimal Model
prerequisites.why_needed: 本章在推导单代响应（育种者方程）时，直接引用LW第4章中关于育种值和无限小模型的基础知识，缺少这些概念无法理解响应计算。
key_points: 理解育种值（A）的定义：亲本传给后代的加性遗传效应
掌握亲本-子代回归和期望子代值等于亲本平均育种值
熟悉无限小模型假设：多基因效应可加且独立
prerequisites.concept_title: Chapter 4 · Breeding Values and Infinitesimal Model
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前章节明确引用LW第4章作为育种值和无限小模型的来源，是推导响应公式的必要基础。

prerequisites.title: Chapter 17 · Parent-Offspring Regression
prerequisites.why_needed: 当前章节在讨论非线性亲本-后代回归时直接引用了LW第17章，理解该内容是掌握选择响应预测的前提。
key_points: 非线性回归可能由主效基因或显性效应引起。
当回归非线性时，仅用选择差S不足以预测后代均值。
亲本群体的方差也会影响选择响应。
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前章节明确引用LW第17章阐述非线性亲本-后代回归。

prerequisites.title: 定量遗传学与遗传力
prerequisites.why_needed: 本章依赖定量遗传学的核心概念，如遗传力、育种值和亲属间的遗传协方差，以预测选择响应。
key_points: 理解遗传力（h²）及其在预测选择响应中的应用
理解亲属间遗传协方差在间接选择中的作用
掌握育种者方程及其选择响应分量
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前章节使用遗传力、遗传协方差和选择响应公式，这些是定量遗传学的核心内容。

prerequisites.title: Chapter 21 · Correlations Between Characters
prerequisites.why_needed: 多元育种方程中的G和P矩阵涉及性状间相关，需要理解性状相关性的基础知识。
key_points: 性状相关性是多元遗传分析的基础。
理解协方差矩阵与相关矩阵的关系。
掌握如何估计和解释遗传相关。
了解相关对选择响应的影响。
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 第21章关于性状间相关的内容是理解多元育种方程中G和P矩阵的关键前提。

prerequisites.title: Chapter 26 · Mixed Model
prerequisites.why_needed: 本章使用第26章引入的混合模型进行BLUP选择，理解该模型是掌握本节约育种值估计的关键。
key_points: 混合模型包括固定效应和随机效应
育种值a服从MVN(0, σ²A)
通过关系矩阵A连接个体
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前章节明确引用LW第26章介绍的基本混合模型用于BLUP选择。

prerequisites.title: Chapter 8 · 线性回归与亲本-后代回归
prerequisites.why_needed: 第13章大量使用线性回归（尤其是亲本-后代回归）和选择差、选择梯度等概念，这些概念在第8章中有详细介绍和推导。
key_points: 线性回归的斜率等于协方差除以方差，这是选择梯度计算的基础。
亲本-后代回归的斜率是遗传力（h²）的估计值，直接用于预测响应。
多元回归的矩阵形式（P⁻¹S）需要熟悉矩阵运算和多元线性回归。
prerequisites.concept_title: Chapter 8 · 线性回归与亲本-后代回归
prerequisites.evidence_summary: 当前章节核心公式（如选择梯度β=S/σz²和多元矩阵形式β=P⁻¹S）直接依赖第8章的回归理论。

prerequisites.title: Example A6.3 · Selection gradient as gradient of log mean fitness
prerequisites.why_needed: 该附录示例直接给出了选择梯度β等于对数平均适应度对性状均值的梯度，这是理解第13章中多元育种者方程的关键数学基础。
key_points: 选择梯度β = P^{-1}S 等于对数平均适应度对性状均值向量的梯度。
该关系来自Lande 1979a，在多元正态分布假设下成立。
为第13章中关于选择梯度与平均适应度变化的关系提供了数学推导。
